0.text:
User-facing changes in each release, newest first. Each release has a
short summary; expand it for the itemised entries, where breaking changes
come first. Each release's GitHub page lists every merged pull request.
0.title: Changelog

1.text: The request trailers a service layer passes on are validated as a client's before they reach an origin, and captures are written as JSON lines for line-oriented shippers. Details
1.title: Unreleased

2.text: The service layer protocol is roxy.layer.v7, incompatible with roxy.layer.v6. A direction subscribed head is a head alone each way, with no end message after it, and an observe stream is one way: the service sends no heads, bytes or ends on it, and sends close when it is done. A WASM layer subscribed head passes on that direction's head alone: bytes or trailers in the body it gives fail the exchange closed. A service subscribed head no longer gets a content-length on that direction's head, as a WASM layer never did (#592).The flow log's forward_aborted, answer_aborted and upstream_aborted reasons are one, layer_aborted. A cut that follows a fault or the client's loss is no longer a layer's abort, so a body cut on its way through a layer is the client's or the upstream's. A layer's answer is its own when it gives it before taking the response from upstream, whether or not that response had arrived (#593).A raw backtick in an HTTP/1 request path is rejected with invalid_path instead of being percent-encoded; HTTP/2 already refused it. In a query it is still percent-encoded to %60 (#582).Capture is written to capture.jsonl with one JSON object per line, in place of capture.rxc and its length-framed records: the head nested under head, body bytes base64 under data, and at most 48 KiB of body per line. A line-oriented shipper such as Vector or Fluent Bit can take the file as it is (#527).
2.title: Breaking

3.text: A service layer's request trailers are held to a client's rules on their way to an origin: refused without http.allow_request_trailers, held to limits.max_header_bytes, and never a framing, routing, authentication or content-* field. A section that breaks them is the layer's invalid_request: the exchange is refused 503 layer_error, or the error is logged if the origin has already answered, and the origin never sees the request complete. More than limits.max_headers fields is a service protocol violation (#581).An HTTP/2 client's request trailer section is held to limits.max_header_bytes, as an HTTP/1.1 client's chunked trailer section is; one over it is a stream reset, parse_error reason head_too_large (#581).HTTP/1.1 request trailers also meet the byte limit after normalisation, so a pass-through layer is not blamed for the client's oversized section (431, parse_error reason head_too_large).A request held across the policy's valid_until, by an addon or while its body is buffered for inspection, is denied _expired when it reaches the rules, as a request sent after the instant is (#568).Without forwarded_for, client.ip is the canonical TCP peer address: an IPv4 client on a dual-stack [::] listener is a.b.c.d, not ::ffff:a.b.c.d, in metric keys, the flow log and the addon principal. Rule comparisons already treated the two as one address. client.peer.ip in the flow log keeps the socket's form (#579).JSON the node cannot parse, whether the node.token record, an enrolment or renewal response, a lease or a flow upload's acknowledgement, is reported by the kind of fault and its line and column, never by quoting the input, which could put a token or a lease secret in the log (#532).
3.title: Fixed

4.text: Addons can now answer early and hold a request or response for approval, with the request and response lanes of an exchange living independent lives. This is a breaking change for addons: the service protocol is roxy.layer.v6 and the WASM interface is roxy:addon@0.3.0. Details

5.text: The service layer protocol is roxy.layer.v6. It is incompatible with roxy.layer.v5 and the experimental roxy.layer.v0, and roxy does not accept a v5 peer: both sides must handle stop, trailers, explicit ends in both directions and headless completion. The bundled Python helper implements the new contract (#558).The WASM addon interface is roxy:addon@0.3.0. Components built against 0.2.x or the unversioned package must be rebuilt with the matching SDK and WIT (#558).
5.title: Breaking

6.text: An addon can answer before forwarding, hold a request or an upstream response while it decides, and stream approved content into an answer it has already started. An approval addon can send 200 text/event-stream with keepalive comments while it holds a request or a tool-call event, then approve, edit or deny it (#558).The request and response lanes of an exchange have independent lifetimes: a layer can end or stop one without the other, and an upstream head that arrives after an early answer is still delivered to the addon (#558).Trailers pass through service layers and WASM host-side passthrough, so gRPC status trailers survive an addon stack. WASM byte-stream rewriting has no trailer API and the Python forwarding helpers do not send trailers (#558).
6.title: Added

7.text: Upstream informational responses such as 103 Early Hints are discarded, with or without addons, and an addon cannot publish an informational head (#558).A WebSocket upgrade reserves its relay resources before the 101 reaches the client (#558).Publishing a second outgoing head on a lane is a layer failure and cuts an answer already in progress (#558).A layer that fails while handling a core denial may produce a 503, but the flow record keeps the original deny rule and reason; the layer fault gets its own event (#558).The final flow record for an exchange waits for both lanes' bodies, their validation and every accepted host call to finish (#558).The quickstart's sentinel sidecar streams a model response to the agent as it arrives, holding only each tool call's block while the sentinel judges it, instead of the whole response until the stream ends. A rejected call is replaced by its note in place, and modify now works on streamed responses (#563).A body that streams through a layer costs more CPU per byte than it did; the fixed cost of a layer is unchanged. Tracked in #561.
7.title: Changed

9.text: Quarantine, a bearer-token node protocol, host services for service layers and X-Forwarded-For support, plus two security fixes (GHSA-4297-w88p-8xqv, GHSA-pwq9-p79h-pg35). Breaking for control planes, service layers (roxy.layer.v5), client.port users and the per-addon state store. Details

10.text: Node protocol: a node's credential is a rotating bearer token instead of a client certificate. Enrolment returns token, not_after and renew_after_seconds; later requests send Authorization: Bearer; the state dir holds node.token in place of node.crt and node.key. A control plane built for mutual TLS no longer works (#528).The service layer protocol is roxy.layer.v5: the open message carries the layer's grants and config, and a service may send host-service calls on its stream (#526).client.port is removed as a rule field and metric key. The flow log keeps the TCP peer as client.peer: { ip, port }, so client.port moves to client.peer.port in the log (#525).The per-addon state store and the addons[].state block are gone: a WASM layer's state-get and state-put use the store the rules read with state[..], sized by limits.max_state_entries. A state-put without a TTL gets one hour, not six (#511).Stricter YAML: yes, no, on and off are not booleans, << merge keys and custom tags are errors, and a file holds one document (#482).
10.title: Breaking

11.text: Quarantine: a rule's quarantine action or a listener's quarantine_on.parse_errors threshold puts the proxy into a durable state where every exchange is refused 403 _quarantined. The trip is written to <state-dir>/quarantine and survives a restart; an operator removes the marker, or in node mode the control plane names the incident in the lease's quarantine.release list. roxy run --config accepts --state-dir, required when the config uses quarantine (#505).A layer of either kind can quarantine the proxy through the new quarantine capability: flow.quarantine for WASM, a quarantine message for a service (#529).Service layers get the host services WASM layers have: log, record, add_tag, state_get, state_put and metric_get messages, each answered with a result; capabilities and config are accepted on a service layer (#526).An http listener takes forwarded_for: { trusted_hops: N } to recover the client IP from X-Forwarded-For; the result is client.ip everywhere. A header with too few entries or a malformed trusted entry is refused 400 forwarded_for_invalid. The setting is a config error on an http_proxy listener (#525).Node protocol: the lease poll reports seq_unreserved when the node could not persist its flow sequence counter (#502).The docs site publishes each release under /vX.Y/ with a version menu (#522).
11.title: Added

12.text: The rule language calls a field admission when it is known at the forwarding decision and in-flight when it is re-checked as the exchange streams, in place of "head" and "watched"; roxy check, rule test and the compiler diagnostics use the new words (#524).A tag an enforce layer adds is visible to tag[..] in admission and in-flight rules and to the when of the layers below; the 64-tag / 4 KiB cap now counts the rules' tags too (#534).The wait for a busy layer instance is bounded by the layer's first_byte_timeout; past it the exchange fails closed with layer_error kind no_instance (#513).The health and CA listener has its own connection cap, so a client filling limits.max_connections on the proxy port cannot starve /healthz (#503).roxy check warns about a metric keyed on host or client.port without a where, with field-specific advice, and no longer warns for unique(..) fields (#497).The WIT package is roxy:addon@0.2.1, an additive bump that 0.2.0 components still load. The SDK's flow::metric_get loses its key parameter (#542).Node mode: a 401 on /renew is retried with backoff rather than ending renewal; 410 or 426 at enrolment is reported as a refusal (#546).A service observe stream ends on the service's last message rather than roxy's, with first_byte_timeout to send it, so a service observer can read a body and then record. Host calls queued before a stream ends still run (#548).A layer's own body that is still open splices the bypassed body as unknown length, so a held-back end or a failure is always a visible cut. A head-only WASM request layer that passes a stream to next now sends a chunked request upstream (#543).The node reserves flow sequence numbers off the emit path, so a slow disk no longer stalls every emitter (#485).
12.title: Changed

13.text: A WebSocket through a layer subscribed to (request: full, response: head) no longer stalls (#516).A service-layer head with too many header fields is refused at limits.max_headers instead of panicking (#499).Client parse-error detail is redacted in the operational log as it is in the flow log (#498).
13.title: Fixed

14.text: GHSA-4297-w88p-8xqv: Host: [::ffff:1.2.3.4] bypassed a deny on 1.2.3.4. An IPv4-mapped IPv6 literal now parses as the IPv4 address it embeds, and a host or tls.sni literal written in the mapped form is a compile error (#506).GHSA-pwq9-p79h-pg35: with http.allow_obs_text: true, a header value holding a byte of 0x80 or above was invisible to an equality rule but forwarded. Rules now read header values as the bytes that are forwarded, one character per byte (#507).YAML is read with serde-saphyr; the unmaintained unsafe-libyaml (RUSTSEC-2024-0449) is gone (#482). ruzstd 0.9.1 for RUSTSEC-2026-0344 (#505).
14.title: Security

15.text: Heads cross the WASM boundary as records and bodies as bare streams (roxy:addon@0.2.0), layers subscribe to only the directions they need, and a batch of host hardening fixes. Breaking for WASM components and service layers (roxy.layer.v4). Details

16.text: The WASM addon interface is roxy:addon@0.2.0: a head crosses the guest boundary as one record per direction and bodies are bare wasi:io streams; the wasi:http import is gone. Components must be rebuilt against SDK 0.2.0, which is source-compatible (#424).The service layer protocol is roxy.layer.v4: the deny message is gone (a service refuses by answering with a response) and open carries the layer's subscription (#420).Removed audit_endpoint, the audit flag of flow.record, endpoint retries and the attempts field of the endpoint_call event (#420).Removed the dead transparent-listener keys (mode: transparent, allow_passthrough, upstream_target); they are now unknown-field errors (#457).A host or tls.sni literal that can never match (trailing dot, non-ASCII, bracketed IPv6) is a compile error with a rewrite hint (#463).
16.title: Breaking

17.text: A layer declares what it wants of each direction with subscribe: { request: head | full, response: head | full }. A body a layer is not subscribed to bypasses it; bytes it passes on for that body fail the exchange closed (#420).SECURITY.md, pointing at private vulnerability reporting (#464).
17.title: Added

18.text: first_byte_timeout is one budget per head, request and response alike, for WASM layers as it already was for service layers (#431).Service layer streams spread across up to max_connections connections instead of filling one, and writes are flushed in batches (#423).The addon SDK moves bodies and heads a layer does not touch host-side, cutting a no-op layer's cost (#418).A fault after the response head carries its own reason into the request event (buffer_budget_exhausted, upstream_body_failed, layer_error or the client's parse reason) instead of response_write_failed (#419).like patterns are capped at 1 KiB and compiled with the same limits as matches; ? matches one character, as documented (#459).
18.title: Changed

19.text: A guest head with tens of thousands of header fields is refused at limits.max_headers instead of panicking the host (#458).A guest that writes to stdout or stderr no longer fails every exchange through its layer (#469).A handler that returns without responding is treated like a trap: the instance is discarded and the exchange fails (#460).An endpoint call waits for its in-flight permit before its body leaves the guest (#465).A service connection whose write side has died fails its exchanges at once with service:closed instead of after first_byte_timeout (#461).Body frames on an ended service stream are dropped without crediting, so a misbehaving service cannot grow roxy's memory (#462).response_body_idle_timeout applies while a response body is collected for inspection; a stalled upstream under a body rule gets a 504 (#467).The reference says what the code does where it overclaimed: timeouts, drain and linger limits, the hop-by-hop list, node 410 handling and lease fields (#457); HTTP/1.0 close-delimited responses are documented (#466).
19.title: Fixed

20.text: The first release: a strict, programmable HTTP firewall. Two ways to deploy it: as an egress proxy for a workload you don't trust (mode: http_proxy, with TLS terminated by roxy's own CA), or as a gateway in front of the APIs your clients call (mode: http).One canonical form: every request is parsed into one strict model and re-serialised, over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2, with WebSockets relayed. Anything roxy cannot parse, verify or classify is denied.A typed YAML rule language where deny always wins and nothing unlisted passes; rules can watch bodies and WebSocket messages as they stream. Metrics give rate limits and byte budgets; secret injection and AWS SigV4 signing mean clients hold only placeholders.Addons above the rules, as WASM components in process or external services streamed over WebSocket: they can rewrite, withhold, answer or block, and the rules judge whatever they pass on.A JSONL flow log naming the rule or addon behind every decision, with optional body capture and digests; backpressure holds traffic until the log catches up.Node mode: roxy enrols with a control plane, leases its policy and secrets into memory, and ships its flow log.

21.text: roxy is a strict, programmable HTTP firewall. Requests and responses stream through addons that can rewrite, hold, answer or block them, then through rules that decide what is forwarded. Anything roxy cannot parse, verify or classify is denied (how roxy works).
21.title: Overview

22.text: Sandbox containment. An untrusted workload's only route out is roxy. It sets HTTPS_PROXY to roxy and trusts roxy's CA. roxy decrypts each request, decides on it, injects credentials the workload never sees, and logs every decision (sandbox containment). HTTP gateway. Clients send requests to roxy directly, behind a load balancer that terminates TLS. Rules route each request by host and inject the real API keys, so clients only hold placeholders (HTTP gateway).
22.title: Use cases

23.text: The quickstart runs generated traffic through roxy with an auth check, a per-user token quota and an inspect_sentinel sidecar. It needs no API key. examples/human-approval runs Claude Code behind roxy and holds every tool call until someone clicks Approve or Deny in the browser.
23.title: Try it

24.text: roxy is open source, written in Rust, and dual-licensed under Apache 2.0 and MIT. Outstanding work is tracked in issues.

25.text:
Addons are listed under addons:, in the order the request passes through them
(addon model). Each entry is a WASM layer or a
service layer; the two kinds share most keys. addons:

    kind: wasm
    path: /etc/roxy/addons/sentinel.wasm
    mode: enforce
    when: host == "api.anthropic.com" and path starts_with "/v1/messages"
    subscribe: { request: full, response: head }
    capabilities: [state, record, endpoints]

30.text:
An addon can only reach roxy's host services that its capabilities
grant: capabilitygrantsendpointscalls to the addon's endpoints. A service layer does not need it: it makes its own callsstatereading and writing the state storerecordwriting events to the flow logmetricsreading metricslogwriting to roxy's own logquarantinequarantining roxy; enforcing addons only Calling a service without its capability fails the addon. Reading the
exchange's details, adding tags and reading config need no capability,
but observers cannot add tags or write state. There is no capability for
secrets: credentials go in an endpoint's headers.
30.title: Capabilities

31.text:
subscribe sets what an addon gets of each direction. With full, the
default, the addon reads the body as it streams, and what it passes on is
the body that goes on. With head, the addon only gets the head, and the
body goes past it untouched. A head-only addon can still refuse, change or answer at the head. If it
answers a response head with the status it was given, the upstream's
body follows. If it answers with another status, its own (empty) body
replaces the upstream's.A head-only addon cannot send a body of its own; trying to fails the
exchange (unsubscribed:request or unsubscribed:response).A head-only observer costs no buffering.The rules judge the request that leaves the stack, head and body,
whoever supplied each.
31.title: What a layer sees

32.text:
An observer gets copies of the traffic and runs beside the exchange,
which does not wait for it. An observer that keeps up sees every body in
full. It loses its copy, and the exchange carries on, if it falls
limits.max_observer_lag_bytes behind, if the
buffer budget runs out, or if no
instance is free within its first_byte_timeout. Each of these logs an
observer_lagged event.
32.title: Observers

33.text:
Bodies stream through addons chunk by chunk, so streaming protocols work: protocolnotesSSE, NDJSON, streaming JSON, multipart, HTTP-based MCPChunk boundaries need not match the protocol's messages, so an addon that edits messages has to parse them itself.gRPCWorks, including trailers such as grpc-status. A WASM addon that copies a body into a new stream drops its trailers; passing the body through keeps them.WebSocketsSupported over HTTP/1.1 (below).1xx responsesNot relayed. An addon sends one final response head.other upgrades, raw TCP, WebTransport, HTTP/3Not supported. An addon that holds a streaming response for approval can send its own
200 text/event-stream head straight away, keep the connection alive
with SSE comments such as : approval pending, and then stream the
approved events. Once the head has gone, a refusal has to be an event in
the stream, not a new status.
33.title: Streaming protocols

34.text:
when is a rule language condition. An
addon runs only on the exchanges it matches, and the rest pass it at no
cost. when sees the request as it reaches the addon, after earlier addons
have changed it.It can read request fields, state, metrics and address lists, but not
bodies, responses or WebSocket messages.tag["x"] sees tags set by earlier addons, not by the rules, which run
later.If an input it needs is unavailable, the exchange fails with 503
rather than skipping the addon. sample is decided from the exchange's id, so the same exchange always
gets the same answer.

35.title: In the flow log

36.text:
When an addon that reads bodies runs on an exchange, roxy decompresses
the bodies for it and removes content-encoding. The client then gets an
uncompressed response and the upstream an uncompressed request. Nothing
is compressed again. A body in a coding roxy does not know, or a partial
response (206), passes through as it is. http.decode_for_addons: false turns this off, so addons see bodies as
sent.
36.title: Content codings

37.text:
An addon gets a WebSocket's upgrade request like any other request, and
the upstream's 101 as the response. After that, the request body
carries the client's WebSocket frames and the response body the
upstream's, for as long as the WebSocket is open. The addon can read,
change or hold either direction, or refuse the upgrade by answering it. The addon must handle both directions at once, since the request body
only ends when the client closes. The roxy-addon SDK does this.Frames from the client are masked, as the WebSocket protocol requires.An addon that turns the 101 into another status fails the exchange.
37.title: WebSockets

38.text:
Every failure is closed. If an enforcing addon crashes, goes over a
limit, uses a capability it lacks, passes on an invalid head, or never
answers, the exchange fails: with 503 and terminal_rule:
layer:<name> if the response has not started, and otherwise by closing
the connection before the response is complete. A layer_error event
records what went wrong in kind, such as trap, budget:<limit>,
capability:<name>, invalid_request, invalid_response,
no_response or service:<code>. A client that disconnects cancels the exchange; that is not the addon's
failure. A WASM instance that failed is thrown away, never reused. An addon that deliberately stops a body part way through, for example by
dropping a stream without finishing it, is not a failure. Nor is one that
stops reading the response from upstream, which cancels the request
upstream. The flow log records layer_aborted, and whoever reads that
body sees it end early.
38.title: Failure

39.text:
Only one party is blamed for a failed exchange: the first to fail. An addon's own failure is that addon's. A request an addon passed
on that is invalid is blamed on that addon.A client upload that breaks is the client's, as without addons,
even if an addon passed the broken body on.An upstream response body that fails is the upstream's
(upstream_body_failed).A body the buffer budget cannot cover is the budget's
(buffer_budget_exhausted).An observer is never blamed.
39.title: Who is blamed

40.text:
Rules decide by name. The address floor decides by IP address: before
roxy connects to an upstream, it checks every address the name resolved
to. Private addresses are refused by default, and address lists let you
refuse more. The settings are under upstream and address_lists
(upstream).
40.title: Address floor and lists

41.text:
roxy refuses to connect to an address if: it is in deny_cidrs, which nothing can override; orit is in one of the private ranges below, deny_private_ranges is on
(the default), the address is not in allow_cidrs, and the rule that
allowed the request does not say private_ok: true; orit is in one of the lists named in deny_lists, which nothing can
override. classrangesunspecified0.0.0.0/8, ::private10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16 (RFC 1918)shared100.64/10 (CGNAT)loopback127/8, ::1link_local169.254/16, fe80::/10documentation192.0.2/24, 198.51.100/24, 203.0.113/24, 2001:db8::/32benchmarking198.18/15multicast224/4, ff00::/8reserved192.0.0/24, 240/4unique_localfc00::/7site_localfec0::/10discard100::/64 The check is on the address roxy actually connects to, so DNS rebinding
does not get around it. It applies to IP addresses in URLs, redirect
targets and addon endpoints too. An IPv4 address can be written as an IPv6 address in several ways, for
example ::ffff:10.0.0.1, or through NAT64 (64:ff9b::/96) or 6to4
(2002::/16). Denies match all of these forms. allow_cidrs only matches
the plain form of an address, so it cannot be used to sneak a private
address through. A refused connection gets 403 with terminal_rule: _address_policy, and
an upstream_denied event in the flow log names the address and the
range or list that matched.
41.title: Address floor

42.text:
Address lists are named sets of IP ranges. They can be used to refuse
connections (upstream.deny_lists) and in rules, as @name. address_lists:
  - name: blocked
    file: /etc/roxy/lists/blocked.txt    # one address or CIDR per line; `#` comments
  - name: cloud-metadata
    inline: [169.254.169.254/32, "fd00:ec2::254/128", 100.100.100.200/32] In rules, use @name after in or not in with an IP field:
client.ip in @internal. In a rule, a list only matches the plain form
of an address, since a rule may allow on it.Lists are fast to search: a million entries take about 11 MiB.A file larger than limits.max_address_list_bytes (256 MiB), or with a
malformed line, fails to load.List files are watched and reloaded with the config.roxy check reports how many entries each list has. In

43.text: This runs clients through roxy with three controls on every model call: an addon that authenticates the client, an addon that holds each user to a token quota, and an inspect_sentinel sidecar that blocks tool calls matching a denylist. roxy gets its policy and the model's API key from a small control plane (node mode). The model is scripted and the traffic generated, so nothing needs an API key. The setup is in examples/quickstart.
43.title: Quickstart

46.text: docker compose up --build --attach traffic The first run builds the images, which takes a few minutes. Ctrl-C stops the stack. It runs: controlplane: gives roxy its config, roxy.yaml, and the model's API key, and prints the flow log roxy sends back.roxy: the proxy, on 127.0.0.1:3128.fake-model: a scripted model API. It refuses requests without the API key, which only roxy has.auth-service: knows alice-secret as alice and bob-secret as bob.quota-board: the quota service. Each user has 600 tokens, refilling at five a second.sentinel: the inspect_sentinel sidecar.inspect-view: Inspect's log viewer.traffic: the clients. Alice calls every six seconds, bob every twenty, and mallory, whom the auth service does not know, every thirty.
46.title: Start the stack

47.text: Each client uses the Anthropic SDK through roxy, with its credential in an x-roxy-auth header. The scripted responses include a Bash tool call that runs curl, which the sentinel blocks: traffic-1  | [alice #2] I will fetch that page for you. roxy's sentinel blocked a Bash tool call (denylist match: 'curl'). Responses stream to the client as the model produces them, except tool calls. The sentinel holds each tool call until its arguments are complete, then lets it through or replaces it with a note. Mallory is refused by the auth check: traffic-1  | [mallory #1] 401 AuthenticationError: credential refused by the auth service Within the first minute alice uses up her tokens, and her calls are refused until they refill: traffic-1  | [alice #8] 429 RateLimitError: token bucket empty (600 tokens, refills 5/s); try again in 15s
47.title: Watch the traffic

48.text:
Open http://127.0.0.1 to see each user's tokens. To make a call of your own: docker compose run --rm client --user bob
docker compose run --rm client --user mallory --secret wrong
48.title: Watch the quota board

49.text: Open http://127.0.0.1. Each client is a sample. Its transcript shows every model call, the tool calls, and the sentinel's verdict on each. Reload the page to see new calls.
49.title: Watch it in Inspect View

50.text: docker compose logs roxy Each request has one line: the rule it matched, the addons it went through, the user:alice tag the auth check set, and the x-api-key header the rule added. The addons' calls to their services are logged too. The control plane receives the same events every few seconds; docker compose logs controlplane shows them.
50.title: Read roxy's flow log

51.text: roxy's policy is valid for sixty seconds and refreshed every fifteen. Stop the control plane: docker compose stop controlplane Within a minute the policy expires and every call fails with 403. docker compose start controlplane brings a fresh policy and roxy recovers without a restart.
51.title: Stop the control plane

52.text: Ctrl-C in the terminal running up, then: docker compose down -v
52.title: Clean up

53.text: An exchange passes through the addons in the order roxy.yaml lists them, then the rules. The auth check (addons/auth-gate) asks the auth service who the x-roxy-auth credential belongs to, tags the exchange user:alice, removes the header and passes the request on. An unknown credential is answered 401.The token quota (addons/token-quota) asks the quota board whether the user has tokens left and answers 429 if not. As the response streams it reads the token usage and reports it to the quota board. Usage is only known after the response, so a user can go over by one call.The sentinel is a service layer: an addon that runs in its own process. It checks every tool call in a model response with inspect_sentinel. The rules then allow exactly one request, POST /v1/messages on the model host, and add the real API key from a secret. A request the addons skip is one the rules deny. If an addon cannot do its job, for example because its service is down, the exchange fails with 503. Stop the quota board (docker compose stop quota-board) to see it. To run roxy from a config file instead of the control plane: docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.standalone.yaml up --build --attach traffic
53.title: What just happened

54.text: The sentinel blocks tool calls matching a regular expression from policies.py. The default catches curl, wget, nc, ncat, ssh, scp, rsync and rm -rf. Set your own with SENTINEL_DENY: SENTINEL_DENY='\bls\b' docker compose up --attach traffic

59.text:
Common HTTP servers resolve framing ambiguities that the HTTP/1.1 spec
lets a server resolve, such as Transfer-Encoding alongside
Content-Length. A proxy that resolves an ambiguity one way while the
origin behind it resolves it another way can be used to smuggle requests.
roxy refuses these requests instead, and its own parser gives every
refusal a stable reason code
(rejection rules). HTTP/2 framing has
no such ambiguities, so roxy uses an existing HTTP/2 implementation.
59.title: Why roxy parses HTTP/1.1 itself

60.text:
Exchange: one request and its response, or one WebSocket session.
Also called a flow; each has an id in the flow log.Canonical: roxy's validated, normalised form of a request.Admission rule, in-flight rule: a rule decided before the request is
forwarded, which can allow or deny, versus one checked as the exchange
streams, which can only deny or add effects.Policy: the compiled config, swapped in whole on reload.Layer: one addon in the stack.Address floor: the check on every upstream address before roxy
connects (address floor).

65.text:
One YAML file, starting version: 1. Each section is described on the
page the table names. keypagelisteners, httpHTTPca_server, tlsmanaging the CA, TLSupstreamupstream, address flooraddress_listsaddress listslimitsresource limitsrulespolicy evaluation, rule languagesecretssecretsmetricsrate limitsaddonsaddon configurationlog, capture_dirflow logvalid_untillease Parsing is strict. An unknown key, or a key repeated in one map, is an
error.Only true and false are booleans; yes, no, on and off are
refused. Anchors and aliases work; merge keys (<<) and custom tags do
not. A file holds one YAML document.Relative paths resolve against the working directory.roxy check refuses zero for a limit where zero would refuse every
request. Body, message and capture caps and timeouts accept zero and
mean it (resource limits). version: 1

listeners:
  - name: proxy
    mode: http_proxy      # the default; `http` serves origin-form requests directly
    bind: 0.0.0.0:3128

secrets:
  openai: { env: OPENAI_API_KEY }
  gh:     { file: /run/secrets/github_token }   # one trailing newline stripped
  lease:  { lease: true }                       # supplied by the control-plane lease; standalone `run` refuses it

metrics:
  - id: github_writes
    count: requests
    where: host under "api.github.com" and method in [POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE]
    key: [client.ip]
    window: 1m

rules:
  - id: github-reads
    when: host under "github.com" and method in [GET, HEAD]
    then: allow

  - id: openai
    when: host == "api.openai.com" and path starts_with "/v1/" and method == POST
    then:
      - set_header: { authorization: "Bearer ${secret:openai}" }
      - allow

  - id: no-writes-burst
    when: metric.github_writes >= 30
    then: { deny: { status: 429 } }

  - id: upload-cap               # reads body.bytes: re-checked in flight
    when: host == "api.openai.com" and body.bytes > 10mb
    then: { deny: { status: 413 } }

69.text:
Secret values that roxy injects are removed from everything it logs. The
values of authorization, proxy-authorization, cookie, set-cookie
and x-api-key are never logged, and log.redact_headers adds more.
Query values are redacted.
69.title: Redaction

70.text:
The flow log never drops a record while roxy runs
(audit backpressure). One thread writes each log file, in batches, so a record is written
within a few milliseconds.When more than log.flow.high_water (8 MiB) is waiting to be written,
or the disk fails, roxy holds traffic until the log catches up.With max_file_bytes, the file is rotated to
<path>.<UTC timestamp>-<seq>, optionally gzipped, and files beyond
max_files are deleted. SIGHUP reopens the file, for external
rotation.On shutdown roxy writes everything queued, retrying a failing
destination for up to 10 seconds. Records still unwritten after that are
lost.roxy does not fsync, so a power loss can lose recent records. log:
  redact_headers: []
  flow:
    path: /var/log/roxy/flow.jsonl  # absent = stdout
    connection_events: false
    ws_message_every: 0             # also log every Nth WebSocket message; 0 = denied only
    high_water: 8mb                 # at least 64kb
    max_file_bytes: 100mb           # absent = never rotate
    max_files: 10                   # absent = keep all
    compress: true Rotation needs path, since stdout cannot be rotated.
70.title: Writing

71.text:

<capture_dir>/capture.jsonl. It records the exchanges a rule selects
with capture: request | response | both, or every exchange with
log.capture.all: true. It is written like the flow log, with the same
batching, rotation and backpressure. Secret values are removed from captured headers and URLs. Bodies are
captured unredacted. capture_dir: /var/lib/roxy/capture   # absent = capture off; restart to change
log:
  capture:
    all: false
    high_water: 64mb
    max_file_bytes: 1gb
    max_files: 20
    compress: true

73.text:
What an addon can ask roxy to do beyond handling its own traffic. Each
service needs a capability granted in the addon's config
(capabilities). A WASM
addon calls them through the flow and endpoints imports. A service
layer sends the matching messages
(service layers). Either way
they behave the same. Size limits are in
fixed caps.
73.title: Host services

74.text:
endpoints.call(name, head, body) sends a request to an endpoint named in
the addon's config. roxy adds the endpoint's configured headers, applies
its timeout, and checks the address floor. The addon cannot choose a
destination of its own and never sees the endpoint's credentials. The
call does not go through the addons or the rules, so a monitor's own
model call is not judged by itself. Each call is logged as an
endpoint_call event. An exchange can have up to 8 calls in progress. A further call waits for
one to finish.The request body is buffered before the call, up to 16 MiB.Failures come back as distinct errors: destination-not-found,
destination-denied, request-uri-invalid, timeout or internal. The endpoint's path setting: pathtargetfixed (default)the configured URL; the path the addon gives is ignoredprefixthe addon's path, normalised, is appended to the configured path. An encoded slash or backslash (%2F, %5C) is refused A path segment starting with .., however it is encoded, is refused
(request-uri-invalid). With prefix, an addon that copies untrusted
text into the path can reach any route under the configured path, with
roxy's credentials attached.
74.title: Endpoints (endpoints)

75.text:
flow.state-get and flow.state-put read and write the
state store that rules use. A key an
addon writes is the same key a rule reads as state["key"], so an addon
can leave a mark for a rule to deny on. Values are strings. Entries
expire after one hour unless the addon sets a TTL. A full store fails the
exchange. Only enforcing addons can write.
75.title: State (state)

76.text:
flow.current() returns the exchange's id, its tags, and the client as
roxy sees it: address, listener and SNI. Key per-client state on these
rather than on headers the client controls. flow.config() returns the
addon's config: as JSON.
76.title: Identity and config

77.text:
flow.record(kind, json) writes a layer_record event to the flow log.
Secret values are removed from it. It waits if the flow log is behind,
and is never dropped.
77.title: Record (record)

78.text:
flow.metric-get(id, []) reads a metric's value for this exchange's own
key. flow.log writes to roxy's own log, tagged with the exchange and the
addon.
78.title: Metrics and log (metrics, log)

79.text:
flow.quarantine() quarantines roxy:
the current exchange and every one after it are refused until an operator
or the control plane lifts it. Use it only when the workload must be
stopped; to refuse one request, answer it. Only enforcing addons can call
it, and a config that grants it needs roxy run --state-dir.
79.title: Quarantine (quarantine)

80.text:

connection rather than letting traffic through
(fail closed).
